blogs.title: GLP-1s and the Myopathy Spectrum: Rhabdo or Autoimmune IMNM?
blogs.description: With GLP-1 receptor agonists everywhere, not all CK bumps are the same. This post contrasts toxic rhabdomyolysis (abrupt CK spike, myalgias, pigmenturia, rapid fall after drug cessation and fluids) with immune-mediated necrotizing myopathy (subacute progressive proximal weakness, dysphagia/dysphonia, rising CK despite withdrawal, MRI edema, biopsy showing macrophage-predominant necrosis). We use the semaglutide IMNM case and a published tirzepatide rhabdomyolysis case to highlight timelines, bedside clues, and therapy responses that should trigger early rheum/neuro referral and biopsy.

blogs.title: When the Myositis Panel Is Negative: Making the Diagnosis in Seronegative IMNM
blogs.description: Up to a third of IMNM is seronegative—so what now when SRP, HMGCR, and the rest are negative? We outline a pragmatic pathway: targeted MRI to pick the biopsy site; biopsy signatures of IMNM (necrotic/regenerating fibers, membrane attack complex deposition, macrophage infiltration with scant lymphocytes); and how to avoid red herrings like isolated low-titer SS-B. We’ll review labs, imaging, and histology cues that raise pretest probability and shorten time to treatment.

blogs.title: Treating Drug-Triggered IMNM: Steroids, IVIG, and Short Tapers Done Well
blogs.description: Drug-associated IMNM may behave differently from idiopathic disease. Using this case, we discuss when to pulse methylprednisolone, add early IVIG for bulbar or severe weakness, and how to monitor CK and function to justify a rapid taper if remission is achieved after drug withdrawal. We also cover infection risk mitigation (the case’s pseudomonal UTI/sepsis), counseling to avoid rechallenge and possible class crossovers, and when to escalate to steroid-sparing agents if relapse occurs.

blogs.title: AST vs ALT vs CK: Sorting Out Transaminase Elevations When Myopathy and NAFLD Coexist
blogs.description: Elevated transaminases in patients with weakness can come from liver or muscle—and both can coexist. We present a bedside approach using CK, aldolase, GGT, bilirubin, platelets, and imaging to attribute AST/ALT correctly, plus how timelines of normalization help. The case illustrates NAFLD with persistent transaminitis despite CK normalization, a trap that can obscure or overcall myopathy; we’ll outline when a liver biopsy adds value and when it doesn’t.

blogs.title: Reading the Heart in Myositis: Troponin, BNP, and CMR Without Overcalling Myocarditis
blogs.description: Cardiac involvement in inflammatory myopathy is real but nuanced. We walk through interpreting modest hs-troponin and BNP elevations, choosing cTnI over cTnT when available, and leveraging cardiac MRI (edema vs late gadolinium enhancement) to separate myocarditis from stress cardiomyopathy or systemic inflammation. The patient’s reversible edema without scar and transient atrial fibrillation anchor a discussion on when to treat, when to watch, and how to follow.

blogs.title: From Anecdote to Signal: How to Do Pharmacovigilance for GLP-1 Adverse Events
blogs.description: One case does not make causality—but it can start the signal. We use the semaglutide–IMNM case to demonstrate applying WHO–UMC causality categories, what constitutes a probable link, and why rechallenge is off the table. Practical tips include what to document, how and where to report, how to counsel patients about warning symptoms (progressive symmetric weakness, dysphagia) without fear-mongering, and when baseline or symptom-triggered CK testing is reasonable.
